briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally While Michigan Operators Find Openings Despite the 24% Tax
briefs.top: Nationally, the DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearing has wrapped with a judge now drafting a recommendation, while Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy clears another durability milestone toward a 2027 launch. Locally, Michigan operators are pushing through the wholesale tax fight with new hospitality concepts, a resolved surveillance dispute for a major chain, and growing political momentum — from both parties — to roll the levy back.

local.text: Jars Cannabis, the 54-store chain spanning Michigan, Arizona and Colorado, struck a deal with Madison Heights to remove a Flock surveillance camera trained on its parking lot, closing out a years-long dispute stemming from the city's 2022 license denial and clearing the way for smoother operations at the location.

Fields Cannary's Muskegon dispensary-restaurant buildout is still moving forward toward a fall opening, proof that ambitious hospitality-driven cannabis retail concepts can still get built in Michigan even as the wholesale tax squeezes margins elsewhere.

GOP gubernatorial candidate John James made repealing or sharply cutting the 24% wholesale tax a plank of his 'Freedom Agenda,' arguing it "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge" — momentum the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association is actively promoting as a state Rep. James DeSana-backed repeal bill also works its way through Lansing.

The Michigan Supreme Court rewrote the rules governing marijuana-related searches this summer, part of a wave of state-level moves that also included Ohio pushing retailers toward manufacturing as a new growth lever — a reminder that regulatory shifts aren't all downside for operators.

The fight over the tax continues on two legal fronts — MiCIA has now filed a second lawsuit alleging unconstitutional 'tax pyramiding' — while enforcement actions like Zaza Recreational's license surrender and Ground Control Michigan's forfeited processor license signal a market shakeout that's clearing weaker players and creating room for better-capitalized operators.

national.text: The DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearing has concluded, with presiding judge Derek Julius now drafting a recommendation on moving cannabis to Schedule III; the final call rests with DEA Administrator Terrance Cole, putting the industry closer than ever to a federal scheduling shift.

Compass Pathways just posted six-month durability data for its psilocybin therapy COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, with its NDA review underway and full submission on track for Q4 2026 — the company is targeting a first-half-2027 launch pending FDA approval and DEA rescheduling.

M&A hit a new gear in August: Curaleaf launched a $4-per-share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, while Vireo Growth's merger with Planet 13 will push Vireo to roughly 265 dispensaries across 15 states once pending deals close — a signal that consolidation is accelerating around scale players.

The FDA has scheduled a hybrid public hearing for September 14 on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs, directly implementing President Trump's Executive Order 14401, which directs federal agencies to accelerate research and drug approvals for psychedelic treatments of serious mental illness.

Consumer demand keeps climbing: Florida set a monthly medical cannabis sales record at $198.2 million and Minnesota's legal market hit $136 million in the first half of 2026, underscoring that legal markets keep expanding even amid regulatory turbulence.
